svg.text: K1b Peeling, coring, stoning: the fixed peeler post and the roll
The roll turns the produce on a spit, the arm draws it past fixed blades on the dump-slot rim. No peeling machine.
3 mechanisms: P1 spit + post, P2 rice in the skin, P3 tubes on the roll axis
post: sprung Y-blade 3–6 N, paring blade with 2.5 / 5 mm shoe, fine rasp
potato: Y-blade at 150 rpm, 15 s each, 15–20 % loss
corer tubes Ø 14 / 22 / 42 on one shank, pushed ≤ 100 N, roll ±30°
P1 SPIT AND POST (side view, front band)
where it sits (top view of the front band, door at the bottom)
dump slot with the post · nests at both ends

g.text: arm draws it pole to pole

svg.text: P3 TUBES ON THE ROLL AXIS: core and eject
the plug stays in the tube;
the pin pushes it into the slot
STONE FRUIT: cut round the stone, twist apart

g.text: on the stone; fruit turned once
free half held in the twist nest, the roll turns 90°: halves part

svg.text: cut at ±7 mm on the edge

g.text: 1/6 The spit fork (three prongs on the roll axis) is pushed along the arm into the potato lying in the stab nest
2/6 The roll spins it at 150 rpm while the arm draws it pole to pole across the sprung Y-blade; the peel falls into the dump slot
3/6 The stripping notch pulls the peeled potato off the prongs into the pot; thick skins use the paring blade with its depth shoe
4/6 Coring: a tube on the roll axis is pushed into the produce in its nest while the roll rocks ±30°; the plug comes out in the tube
5/6 The tube is pressed on the ejector post at the slot: the plug drops into the slot
6/6 Stone fruit: the post edge cuts round the stone as the fruit turns; in the twist nest the roll turns 90° and the halves part
